evidence.claim: The government appointed finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, a long-serving civil servant with more than 18 years in the Finance Division and experience in budget reform and macroeconomic management, as Bangladesh Bank governor.
evidence.title: Bangladesh appoints Abdur Rouf Talukder as central bank governor
evidence.excerpt: The government appointed finance secretary Abdur Rouf Talukder, a long-serving civil servant with more than 18 years in the Finance Division and experience in budget reform and macroeconomic management, as Bangladesh Bank governor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct appointment report with detailed professional background and clear period fit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly about appointment quality.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Hasina government’s appointment choice, though the article does not prove Hasina personally screened the candidate.
contrary_evidence: One technocratic appointment does not erase broader patronage or self-dealing concerns elsewhere in the record.

evidence.claim: A journalist was investigated under the Digital Security Act after publishing a video investigation alleging corruption by a local shrine management committee, and he said politicians and their associates repeatedly threatened him and tried to stop publication.
evidence.title: Bangladeshi journalist Imran Hossain Titu investigated under Digital Security Act
evidence.excerpt: A journalist was investigated under the Digital Security Act after publishing a video investigation alleging corruption by a local shrine management committee, and he said politicians and their associates repeatedly threatened him and tried to stop publication.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A detailed contemporaneous NGO case report with the journalist’s account, dates, and retaliation allegations, though the direct government nexus is still indirect.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and directly about retaliation against corruption reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the governing environment under Hasina because the Digital Security Act and police process were used against a corruption reporter, but the immediate complainant was a local shrine-related actor rather than Hasina herself.
contrary_evidence: The alleged corruption concerned a local shrine committee, so the personal nexus to Hasina is indirect.

evidence.claim: In a BBC interview, Hasina said people should judge for themselves how much truth there is in allegations of enforced disappearances and said free and fair elections were only possible under an Awami League government.
evidence.title: Enforced disappearances: Check before you allege
evidence.excerpt: In a BBC interview, Hasina said people should judge for themselves how much truth there is in allegations of enforced disappearances and said free and fair elections were only possible under an Awami League government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous direct-quote reporting from a major Bangladeshi paper; secondary source but with specific on-record quotations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for the quoted remarks because they are first-person statements by Hasina; low for any inference of admission because the remarks are defensive, not corrective.
contrary_evidence: The quote is not an admission, correction, or disclosure of wrongdoing; it is a denial or deflection.
No self-correction is stated in the passage.

evidence.claim: The article reports that an allocation letter for Hasina's 10-katha Purbachal plot was issued on August 3, 2022, that her son's and daughter's allocation letters were also issued later in 2022, and that related files were allegedly removed from Rajuk records and hidden elsewhere.
evidence.title: HC forms panel to probe plots given to Hasina, family
evidence.excerpt: The article reports that an allocation letter for Hasina's 10-katha Purbachal plot was issued on August 3, 2022, that her son's and daughter's allocation letters were also issued later in 2022, and that related files were allegedly removed from Rajuk records and hidden elsewhere.
evidence.source_locator: article paragraphs describing the allocation chronology and file removal
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific dated record-based reporting with concrete 2022 allocation dates; secondary but highly material to the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Directly ties the allegation to 2022 allocation actions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for the alleged 2022 allocation chronology because it is tied to official RAJUK records and named beneficiaries, though the paper reports allegations and petitions.
contrary_evidence: This remains allegation-stage reporting, not a final court finding.
The file-removal claim is attributed to officials and does not independently prove Hasina's intent.

evidence.claim: The ACC filed a case against Hasina and Saima Wazed alleging irregularities and abuse of power in allocating six 10-katha plots in Purbachal, and ACC director general Akhter Hossain said Hasina abused power to allocate the plots to her and family members.
evidence.title: Irregularities in Purbachal plot allocation: Case filed against Hasina, Saima
evidence.excerpt: The ACC filed a case against Hasina and Saima Wazed alleging irregularities and abuse of power in allocating six 10-katha plots in Purbachal, and ACC director general Akhter Hossain said Hasina abused power to allocate the plots to her and family members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of an ACC filing and DG remarks with specific alleged conduct and beneficiaries.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective corroboration of a 2022 allocation decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for the alleged use of office because the ACC attributes the mechanism to Hasina's power and names family beneficiaries; still not a court judgment.
contrary_evidence: The article reports allegations and a filed case, not a verdict.
Some details depend on ACC claims rather than an adjudicated finding.

unresolved_gaps: No direct Hasina-specific 2022 decision on nuclear safety appointments, command-and-control, or emergency doctrine.
No independent audit of Rooppur safety performance or BAERA independence in the target year.
No direct Bangladesh-initiated interstate war, proxy war, or coercive military campaign in 2022.
Direct command-chain evidence for specific 2022 abuses remains thin.
Stronger direct evidence is still needed on institutional restraint, especially courts, election administration, and oversight bodies.
Household-level distribution and independent execution evidence are thinner than macro and program-announcement evidence.
Direct ruler causation for service delivery is thinner than outcome evidence.
Direct first-person evidence of correction, admission, or disclosure is still thin.
The plot-allocation/self-dealing allegations need stronger independent corroboration or final adjudication.
Independent audits of implementation quality and outcome progress are still limited compared with announced-program evidence.
Direct evidence that Hasina personally monitored, corrected, or replaced ineffective implementers is sparse.
